content.content:
Applied by a reviewer reading the recorded nodes; nothing runs. Read the dependent's recorded decision against each recorded prerequisite in turn, one clause per prerequisite, and state which recorded thing fails — never what the dependent should have written.

(1) Subject. A dependent whose content is still a placeholder, or otherwise records no commitment, leaves the check with no subject to read: fail, naming the placeholder.

(2) The entry the cue is attached to (squvoxyr). The entry the dependent gives the pointer cue to is the ref-path entry squvoxyr records, and the dependent's commitment is that entry's cue; what the entry is, how it is presented as against bare text, and what activating it does are that decision's, not this one's. Fail, naming the element, on any element of the dependent that attaches the cue to something other than that entry; that presents the entry as bare or inert content, withholds, replaces or duplicates it, or moves it out of where that decision puts it; that states an activation, an outcome, a destination, a transport, a message or command, or a rule that resolves, normalizes or opens a path; or that makes the entry, or the cue over it, vary with content.type or content.ref in a way squvoxyr does not state. If squvoxyr records no commitment about such an entry, the use has nothing to be read against: fail, naming that absence.

(3) The record the cue spends (wtywxppt). No element of the dependent contradicts any value wtywxppt records under its element, aspect, state, value or note keys: fail, naming the element and the value, if any element of the dependent forbids, reverses or substitutes a recorded value, or narrows the record by excepting a case it covers.

(4) Layer of the check. No clause demands an outcome, an observable, a file, an element, a class or a style property: the cue and the entry are read in the dependent's own words, and which carrier draws them is not asserted here.

(5) Independence. The check presumes no element of the dependent and no particular clause of a prerequisite; which element is at issue is a finding named only in the check's output. It requires no wording, sentence order or vocabulary of the dependent, invents no rule its prerequisites do not state, and rewriting the dependent without changing what it decides leaves every clause intact.
content.rationale:
The use, edge by edge. plkskmxu relies on squvoxyr for the entry itself: a cue can only be a cue on the entry that a recorded decision already presents, so the gate asks whether the dependent attached its cue to that entry and left the entry and its presentation as squvoxyr records them, instead of re-deciding what the entry is, turning it back into bare or inert content, or sliding an activation, a destination or a path-resolution rule in behind the cue. It relies on wtywxppt for the commitment the cue spends: that record's note carries pointer precision and keyboard reachability, and a pointer cue is that pointer-precision commitment made visible before the click, so the gate asks whether the dependent contradicts the recorded value. Neither use is a restatement of the dependent's wording; both are questions asked of the dependent's recorded text.

Layer placement and form. squvoxyr is an inline prose decision (content.type text, ref inline) and so sits on the natural layer; plkskmxu is likewise a commitment in words, so the squvoxyr use is the evaluation matrix's natural-to-natural cell — evals/natural-to-natural.md, whose check is non-violation: no element of the dependent contradicts the prerequisite, the contradicting element named only in the check's output — copied here as clauses (2) and (3). wtywxppt is a visual-spec: an inline JSON object with a fixed key grammar (element, aspect, state, value, note), so it sits on the structured layer, and the child stays natural; the matrix has no structured-to-natural cell, so that use takes the documented default — the same gate form — and is flagged here for a matrix entry, as mmtznvtw flagged the identical pair for its own dependent and as lvqyqozt and wurvunqu flagged before it. One criterion carries both uses because both ask the same question of the same dependent text — does it stay within the prerequisites it was drawn against — and because two evaluations would gate two layer pairs that resolve to one form.

Why nothing runs. The strictness rule gives a child on the natural layer a check of non-violation and never a demand for behaviour, so no clause probes a rendered cursor, a rendered entry or a target size; and this tree carries no ref-path entry to probe — the webview source holds no entry class for a ref path and no cursor declaration at all, so a runnable check would have to be written against an artifact no decision in this slice changes. Whether the cue is in fact drawn, on which element and through which declaration, is observable only of the code-layer carriers — the panel markup and the stylesheet — and is gated where those become artifacts, not from a node pair that decides a cue in words.

Known scope, stated so the check is not read as stronger than it is. wtywxppt's element field names canvas elements (node/*, edge/*), so on a detail-panel entry the licence it gives is the pointer-precision commitment its note and rationale carry, and not its recorded min 24px value: clause (3) cannot demand a hit target for a ref-path entry, and it does not require the dependent to cite or measure one. Nor can (3) catch a dependent that claimed the keyboard half of that note, because no recorded prerequisite of this node states who owns keyboard reachability, focus or the focus indicator; the check therefore stays at non-violation rather than inventing a rule for the case. Clause (1) makes an unauthored or ref-less subject a named failure rather than a silent pass, which is what lets the criterion be applied once the dependent carries a recorded decision.

The criterion never defines plkskmxu, restates it, or tracks its wording, and it names no endpoint-specific element in advance; it survives the dependent being rewritten without changing what it decides, and it asserts nothing its prerequisites do not state, so it is decidable against the recorded graph alone.
